clue.text: A bit of Charles hidden in the tree

indicators.note: the tree is said to have the letters of a bit of the name concealed and reshuffled within it

parts.note: only a bit of the name is used, so its final pair of letters is set aside

explanation.surface: Something of King Charles lies concealed in a tree, recalling the royal oak.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop ES from CHARLES to leave CHARL, a bit of it, and rearrange those five letters to make the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A larch is a deciduous conifer, a kind of tree.

clue.text: Illumination of the stars

parts.note: the bright stage lamp once used to light leading players, and by extension the public attention that famous performers enjoy

explanation.definitionFit: The old stage lamp burnt quicklime to spotlight performers, so the word came to mean fame itself.

clue.text: Light on a sheer fabrication

parts.note: a ray is a beam of light
taken as written

explanation.surface: A ray of light shines on a pure lie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A sheer fabrication' looks like a lie, but it means a thin manufactured fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Rayon is an artificial silk, a fabric made in a factory, and can be woven sheer.

clue.text: Flowering evergreen wine

definitions.note: an adjective standing for the noun, a flowering plant

parts.note: holly is an evergreen shrub
hock is a white Rhine wine

explanation.surface: A wine flavoured with some blossoming evergreen.
explanation.walkthrough: HOCK is the British name for German white wine from the Rhine.
explanation.definitionFit: The hollyhock is a tall garden plant grown for its flowers.

clue.text: It might be reasonable to suppose that the weasel visits them

definitions.text: It might be reasonable to suppose that the weasel visits them

parts.words: It might be reasonable to suppose that the weasel visits them
parts.note: in the nursery song 'Pop goes the weasel', to pop is British slang for pawning goods, so the weasel goes where goods are pledged for loans

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop Goes the Weasel' is a London song; 'pop' means pawn, and 'weasel' was rhyming slang for a coat that was pawned.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the shops where moneylenders take goods as security, where things are popped.

clue.text: Schism, but apparently not in the pulpit

definitions.text: Schism, but apparently not in the pulpit

parts.words: Schism, but apparently not in the pulpit
parts.note: a schism is a rent or split, and this one belongs to the church seats below the preacher rather than to the preacher's stand

explanation.walkthrough: A rent is a split, so the clue pretends to describe a church split confined to the congregation's seats; in fact it is the fee once paid to reserve a seat in church.
explanation.definitionFit: Churches used to charge parishioners an annual fee for a reserved seat.

clue.text: Where one has to labour bilingually seems to be the long and the short of it

definitions.text: Where one has to labour bilingually seems to be the long and the short of it

parts.words: Where one has to labour bilingually seems to be the long and the short of it
parts.note: the town's name reads as the English word for labours in full followed by the short form of the Latin word for a work

explanation.walkthrough: The name splits as WORKS (English, the long) and OP (short for Latin opus, the short): labour said in two languages. Worksop is a town in Nottinghamshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Worksop is an English market town in Nottinghamshire, the place described.

clue.text: He endures to divide thus

indicators.note: the little word is made to split the Latin word in two, so it goes inside it

parts.note: sic is Latin for thus, as printed after a quoted error
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man who puts up with hardship, told to split things this way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divide' reads like splitting something up, but here it means the word 'to' goes inside the Latin for 'thus' and splits it in two.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoic bears pain or hardship without complaint, as the ancient philosophers taught.

clue.text: This government may be made to go charily

indicators.note: the letters of the following words can be made into something else, a signal to rearrange them

explanation.surface: Rule by the few might be forced into acting warily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be made to' signals that the letters of GO CHARILY are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An oligarchy is rule by a small group of powerful people, a form of government.

clue.text: Guide at the cattle show ?

explanation.definitionFit: To steer is to guide; a steer is a young castrated bull, exhibited at cattle shows.

clue.text: Famous ship that suggests doubt in the nursery

parts.note: may expresses uncertainty, as in 'it may rain'
a plant nursery raises flowers

explanation.surface: A celebrated vessel whose name hints at uncertainty in a children's room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nursery' suggests a children's room, but here it is a place where plants are grown.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mayflower carried the Pilgrim Fathers to America in 1620.

clue.text: Branch of peace

parts.note: the twig a dove brought back to Noah, held out as a sign of reconciliation

explanation.definitionFit: Offering a sprig from this tree is the traditional gesture of peace.

clue.text: Attenuated

parts.note: drawn out thin, as a tall gangling person is

explanation.definitionFit: Attenuated means made thin and drawn out, as a tall thin gangly person looks.

clue.text: Not the most suitable seat for Mr. Speaker

definitions.text: Not the most suitable seat for Mr. Speaker

parts.words: Not the most suitable seat for Mr. Speaker
parts.note: the Speaker of the House of Commons presides from a formal chair, and his job is anything but restful

explanation.walkthrough: The Speaker chairs debates in the House of Commons; a comfortable armchair would hardly suit so demanding a post.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep, comfortable armchair for relaxing in, quite unlike a Speaker's formal seat.

clue.text: Proceed with the game in Hampshire

parts.note: to go is to proceed
a sport is a game

explanation.surface: Carry on with the match in a southern English county.
explanation.walkthrough: Hampshire is a county on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Gosport is a naval town on Portsmouth Harbour, a place in that county.

clue.text: There's nothing stirring in this

parts.note: a description of complete calm, where no movement is to be seen

explanation.definitionFit: It means total quiet and absence of motion.

clue.text: "____ are the glass, the school, the book, Where subjects' eyes do learn" (Shakespeare)

definitions.text: "____ are the glass, the school, the book, Where subjects' eyes do learn" (Shakespeare)

parts.words: "____ are the glass, the school, the book, Where subjects' eyes do learn" (Shakespeare)
parts.note: a line from The Rape of Lucrece about royal sons as examples for their people

explanation.definitionFit: Royal heirs are the models their subjects copy, as the poem's line says.

clue.text: Breaking in

parts.note: a sudden forcible entry or invasion

explanation.definitionFit: An irruption is a violent bursting into a place, an invasion.

clue.text: Where she might recover her senses

indicators.note: read as re-cover, the letters are put back together in a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A place where a woman might come to after fainting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recover' signals that the letters of HER SENSES are rearranged. Sheerness is a port town in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheerness is a town on the Isle of Sheppey in Kent, the place meant.

clue.text: Current way to deceive the French

parts.note: to trick is to deceive
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A present-day method of fooling the French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like an adjective meaning present-day, but it is a noun: a small flow.
explanation.definitionFit: A trickle is a thin, slow flow of liquid.

clue.text: It expresses quality

parts.note: a descriptive word or phrase that names a characteristic of someone

explanation.definitionFit: An epithet is a descriptive term attached to a name, such as 'the Great'.

clue.text: Novel family from S.E.40

parts.note: the family in Galsworthy's saga of novels, with a nod to a London postal district

explanation.definitionFit: Galsworthy's Forsyte Saga follows an upper-middle-class London family across several novels.

clue.text: Source of original habits

parts.note: in Genesis Adam and Eve sewed leaves together as the first clothes

explanation.definitionFit: Its leaves gave Adam and Eve their first garments, the earliest clothing.

clue.text: Taking part in a touching incident

definitions.text: Taking part in a touching incident

parts.words: Taking part in a touching incident
parts.note: being one of two things that crash into each other, so they literally touch

explanation.definitionFit: To be crashing together is to make violent contact.

clue.text: Parisian saint

parts.note: the saint who gave his name to Saint-..., the suburb west of Paris

explanation.definitionFit: Saint Cloud was a Frankish prince turned monk, honoured near Paris.

clue.text: " Why art thou here, Como from the farthest steppe of ?" (M.N.D.)

definitions.text: " Why art thou here, Como from the farthest steppe of ?" (M.N.D.)

parts.words: " Why art thou here, Como from the farthest steppe of ?" (M.N.D.)
parts.note: Titania's question to Oberon in A Midsummer Night's Dream, naming the far land he came from

explanation.definitionFit: The play's fairy king has come from that distant eastern country.

clue.text: Fireside game

explanation.definitionFit: The fire iron kept by the hearth for stirring coals; also a card game played for stakes.

clue.text: Browning questioned the quality of his porridge

definitions.text: Browning questioned the quality of his porridge

parts.words: Browning questioned the quality of his porridge
parts.note: the poem Popularity ends 'What porridge had John' and the poet's surname

explanation.definitionFit: Robert Browning's poem asks what humble fare the young Romantic poet ate.

clue.text: A nymph to adore

indicators.note: the little link implies the letters are turned into the following word, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lovely nature spirit to worship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is the slight hint that ADORE is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An oread is a mountain nymph of Greek myth.

clue.text: A violent blow with a quick stick ?

definitions.text: A violent blow with a quick stick ?

parts.words: A violent blow with a quick stick ?
parts.note: a strong wind, its name split as hurry and cane, a hasty stick

explanation.definitionFit: A tropical storm with very strong winds is the violent blow; its sound splits as hurry plus a cane.

clue.text: I send malt (anag.)

indicators.note: the printed abbreviation tells the solver outright to rearrange the words before it

explanation.surface: A bare instruction to rearrange three words.
explanation.walkthrough: This old-style clue gives no definition, only the anagram of I SEND MALT; the answer means take apart.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismantle is to take apart piece by piece.

clue.text: "6 in order ranged Of tame villatic fowl " (Milton)

definitions.text: "6 in order ranged Of tame villatic fowl " (Milton)

parts.words: "6 in order ranged Of tame villatic fowl " (Milton)
parts.note: a line from Samson Agonistes describing a farmyard's roosts of hens

explanation.definitionFit: Farmyard hens roost and lay in these, ranged in rows.
